title: Turn an equity gap into a testable action
brief: Follow-up after hypertension referral is high near the district centre and much lower in remote catchment areas. The {{exec2}} wants one practical next step.

task.stem: Which action should you recommend first?

options.label: Test transport-linked appointment days in one remote catchment and measure completion plus missed visits.
Publish the district average and avoid subgroup targets.
Move all appointments to the district centre.

task.reasonStem: Why is that the strongest first step?

reasons.label: It targets the observed access mechanism, starts small, and includes outcome and balancing evidence.
Every geographic gap is caused only by transport.
Equity work does not need measurement after implementation.

debrief.correct: Correct. The test is targeted, small enough to learn from, and measures both follow-up and unintended burden.
debrief.wrong: A useful equity response connects the observed gap to a plausible access mechanism, tests one change, and measures whether the gap improves without creating new burden.
debrief.rule_cited: Equity-stratified improvement — act on a plausible mechanism and measure the result.
